subject: Evidence & DPIA: subprocessor data transfers & audit rights
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme-health.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@acme-health.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Art. 28/30 records, DPIA artifacts and subprocessor evidence

Hi Marissa —

We are starting our internal privacy review ahead of a pilot and need the following records from Redwood to complete Acme Health's DPIA and procurement review: 

- Current subprocessor registry (with onboarding dates and jurisdictions)
- GDPR Art. 28/30 documentation or equivalent processing records
- Executive DPIA summary or artifacts showing risk mitigations for processing Special Category health data (if applicable)
- Data transfer mechanisms used (SCCs, adequacy, or other)
- Retention policy and sample retention schedule for processed records
- Confirmation of audit rights (remote review vs. on-site) and whether Redwood allows third-party audits under DPA terms

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated turnaround? We have a preferred deadline of 7 business days if possible. Attaching our DPIA template to show the fields our privacy team needs.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior Legal Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Acme Health

Attachment: Acme_DPIA_template.docx

Also flag any items that would require an NDA or controlled access (SOC 2 report, detailed logs).

Priya — we'll aim to scope and provide an initial package or a timeline by EOD tomorrow. If you need anything faster, call me and I can escalate.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Request: Art. 28/30 records, DPIA artifacts and subprocessor evidence

Hi Priya / Marissa —

We can provide the items you asked for; details below and a few clarifying Qs so we scope the deliverables correctly: 

What we can provide without additional paperwork:
- Subprocessor registry export (CSV) with service description, country, and onboarding date (we will redact contact emails for suppliers upon request).
- Redacted processing map focusing on the pipeline components that handle customer data (we will remove internal IP details).
- Executive DPIA summary that covers data categories, legal basis, main risks and mitigations (redacted to avoid operational detail).
- Retention policy and sample retention schedule for customer data.
- List of data transfer mechanisms in use (SCCs where applicable, plus references to our EU controls).

Items typically provided under controlled access / NDA: 
- SOC 2 Type II report (we provide via secure portal / on NDA),
- Detailed access logs / raw audit trails (we can provide snapshots or redacted extracts; full raw logs are shared under strict procedures),
- On-site audit (we allow third-party auditors under a mutually agreed scope and a signed audit addendum).

Quick clarification requests for Acme: 
1) Do you require on-site audit rights or will a remote evidence review + auditor questionnaire suffice? 
2) For DPIA artifacts, do you need the executive summary only or the full assessment template populated with examples?

Timeline: assuming confirmation of scope, we can deliver a first package (subprocessor CSV + processing map redacted + DPIA exec summary) within 5 business days. SOC 2 access and log extracts would take longer (7–10 business days to provision secure access).

We will attach a draft DPA amendment with our standard auditor and transfer language for review.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_dpa_amendment_draft.docx

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme-health.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@acme-health.com
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Art. 28/30 records, DPIA artifacts and subprocessor evidence

Thanks Rishi — that's helpful. A few follow-ups from our legal/privacy team: 

- Audit scope: Acme prefers to reserve the right to appoint a third-party auditor (our vendor) to perform a remote evidence review; on-site could be considered for high-risk items but is not our first request. Please confirm this is acceptable and what limitations you require (e.g., NDA, redaction rules, pre-approved scope).
- DPIA: executive summary is fine initially; we may follow up requesting a populated DPIA template for a subset of questions.
- Logs: as part of our DPIA we will request sample access/export logs for April 2026 (up to 10 anonymized entries that show processing timestamps, operator role, and data category). Are redacted snippets possible?
- Transfers: if you rely on SCCs for transfers, please include the signed controller-processor addendum or indicate where we can view the standard clause references.

We need the initial package within 7 business days if possible. Please confirm timeline and deliverables.

Thanks,
Priya

Attachment: (Acme_DPIA_template.docx referenced above)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Art. 28/30 records, DPIA artifacts and subprocessor evidence

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the scope clarification. Action plan and what we'll provide: 

1) Subprocessor registry: CSV export attached (file: redwood_subprocessor_registry_20260501.csv). Contains vendor name, service description, country, and onboarding date. We have redacted vendor contact emails.

2) Processing map: redacted PDF attached (processing_map_redacted_20260501.pdf) highlighting the flow of customer data and transform points.

3) DPIA executive summary: attached inline in the shared Drive link (redacted), and we will populate key sections in Acme's template where feasible.

4) Logs: we can provide anonymized sample entries for April 2026 (up to 10 entries) showing timestamp, service component, and action type. Full raw logs require a secure access request and approval; we will provide a redacted snapshot in the initial package.

5) Audit rights: Redwood supports remote evidence reviews by a third-party auditor. On-site audits can be accommodated subject to a mutually agreed audit addendum (NDA + scope + date windows) and reasonable limitation on access to operational infrastructure. We'll propose language in the DPA amendment.

6) SOC 2 Type II: available via our secure portal; we'll provide a download link once an NDA or secure access request is completed.

Estimated delivery: initial package (subprocessor CSV + redacted processing map + DPIA exec summary + anonymized log snippets + draft DPA amendment) within 4 business days (by 2026-05-05). SOC 2 portal access and extended logs within 10 business days.

Please let us know if Acme will accept remote review + anonymized log snippets as the first step — that will speed delivery.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
